key_insight: Drift Field Net learns ocean surface advection fields from satellite and in-situ data, and a physics-informed Lagrangian training step makes particle drift forecasts more accurate.
engineering_relevance: The method can improve operational prediction of floating debris transport in the North Pacific Subtropical Gyre, supporting better cleanup planning and resource deployment.
method: Pretrain a neural network on simulated ocean flow fields.
Fine-tune with an advection-consistent Lagrangian loss to enforce trajectory physics.
Use operational satellite observations as inputs for surface flow prediction.
evidence_signal: On in situ drifter trajectories, DFN lowered 7-day mean positioning error by 20 km versus the operational forecast system, and Lagrangian fine-tuning reduced it by an additional 10 km.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on specific drifter and forecast settings, so generalization to other regions, seasons, or extreme flow conditions may require further validation.
paper_title: Drift Field Net: Learning Ocean Lagrangian advection fields from in-situ and satellite observations
